references.text: Balak takes Balaam to another place to see the people, showing a pattern where Balak repeatedly leads Balaam to high places to curse Israel.
Balak takes Balaam to the top of Peor, which is also a high place with a view over Israel, a parallel attempt to curse the people.
Refers to the high places of Baal (bamot) as sites of idol worship that Israel was commanded to destroy, highlighting the religious significance of the place where Balaam was taken.
Mentions Balaam's fate and his role as a prophet, linking him to the events that began at the high places of Baal.
The prophets of Baal gather on Carmel, another example of Baal worship on high places in Israel.
Refers to incense offerings on the high places of Baal, showing the persistent idolatry associated with such locations.
Refers to Balaam's teaching that led Israel into sin, connecting the events at Bamot-Baal with warnings in the New Testament.
